title: The Life of Jesus
description: The whole life of Jesus in one sitting, from the manger in Bethlehem to the empty tomb and the promise that he is with us always: his childhood, his baptism, forty days in the wilderness, the first disciples, the Sermon on the Mount, his healing, the last supper, the cross and the resurrection. Each chapter closes with a short prayer.

beats.say: He was born in a stable, grew up in a small town, and never travelled far from home. And yet no life has ever changed the world like his.
And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us. This is the life of Jesus, from Bethlehem to the empty tomb.
A young woman named Mary, far from home, in a town so full that there was nowhere left to stay.
And she brought forth her firstborn son, and wrapped him in swaddling clothes, and laid him in a manger; because there was no room for them in the inn.
In the fields nearby, shepherds kept watch over their flock by night. And the angel said unto them: Fear not: for, behold, I bring you good tidings of great joy.
For unto you is born this day in the city of David a Saviour, which is Christ the Lord. Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will toward men.
Later, wise men came from the east, following a star. When they saw the star, they rejoiced with exceeding great joy.
Lord Jesus, you came small and quiet, to a place with no room. Find room in me tonight, and be born in my heart again. Amen.
Every year his family went up to Jerusalem for the Passover. When he was twelve, they started home, and he was not with them.
After three days they found him in the temple, sitting in the midst of the doctors, both hearing them, and asking them questions.
And all that heard him were astonished at his understanding and answers.
His mother said: Son, why hast thou thus dealt with us? And he said: Wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business? And Jesus increased in wisdom and stature, and in favour with God and man.
Father, help me grow the way he grew, in wisdom, and in favour with you. Make my ordinary days your business too. Amen.
For eighteen quiet years he worked as a carpenter in Nazareth. Then, at about thirty, he walked to the river Jordan, where John was baptizing.
John saw him coming, and said: Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world.
And Jesus, when he was baptized, went up straightway out of the water: and, lo, the heavens were opened unto him, and he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove.
And lo a voice from heaven, saying: This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased. Before he had preached a sermon, or done a single miracle.
Father, let me hear what he heard: that I am loved before I have done anything to earn it. Let your Spirit rest on me today. Amen.
Then was Jesus led up of the spirit into the wilderness to be tempted of the devil. And when he had fasted forty days and forty nights, he was afterward an hungred.

The tempter said: If thou be the Son of God, command that these stones be made bread. But he answered: It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.
He was offered the kingdoms of the world, and all the glory of them. Jesus said: Get thee hence, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve.
Then the devil leaveth him, and, behold, angels came and ministered unto him. He was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin.
Lord, you know what my temptations feel like, because you felt them too. When I am hungry and tired, put your word in my mouth. Amen.
By the Sea of Galilee, Jesus saw two brothers, Simon called Peter, and Andrew his brother, casting a net into the sea: for they were fishers.
And he saith unto them: Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.
And they straightway left their nets, and followed him. A boat, a trade, a family business, left on the shore in a single moment.
Jesus, you call ordinary people. Give me the courage to leave whatever nets are holding me, and to follow you tomorrow. Amen.
And seeing the multitudes, he went up into a mountain: and when he was set, his disciples came unto him: and he opened his mouth, and taught them.
Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven. Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted.
Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit the earth. Blessed are they which do hunger and thirst after righteousness: for they shall be filled.
Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy. Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God. Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God.
Lord, I do not feel blessed tonight in all the ways the world counts. Teach me to see your blessing where you said it would be. Amen.
Jesus went about all Galilee, healing all manner of sickness and all manner of disease among the people.
And there came a leper to him, kneeling down to him, and saying unto him: If thou wilt, thou canst make me clean.
No one touched lepers. But Jesus, moved with compassion, put forth his hand, and touched him, and saith unto him: I will; be thou clean.
Jesus, you were never too busy to stop. Put your hand on the sick, the lonely, and the ones no one wants to touch. Begin with me. Amen.
Passing through Jericho, Jesus was surrounded by crowds. A chief tax collector named Zacchaeus, rich and despised, and little of stature, ran ahead and climbed a sycamore tree just to see him.
Jesus stopped under the tree and looked up: Zacchaeus, make haste, and come down; for to day I must abide at thy house. And the crowd murmured.
Zacchaeus stood: Behold, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor; and if I have taken any thing from any man by false accusation, I restore him fourfold. Grace changed him faster than any law.
For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost. Lord, look up into whatever tree I am hiding in, and call me down by name. Amen.
On his last night, he poured water into a basin, and began to wash the disciples' feet. The Master took the place of a servant.
Then he took bread, and gave thanks, and brake it, and gave unto them, saying: This is my body which is given for you: this do in remembrance of me.
Likewise also the cup after supper, saying: This cup is the new testament in my blood, which is shed for you.
A new commandment I give unto you, That ye love one another; as I have loved you, that ye also love one another.
Lord, I remember you tonight: your body given, your blood shed, for me. Teach me to love the way you loved, with a towel in my hands. Amen.
He was arrested in a garden, tried through the night, and condemned at dawn. And he bearing his cross went forth into a place called the place of a skull.
There they crucified him. But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: and with his stripes we are healed.
His mother stood near the cross, with the disciple whom he loved. Even there, he made sure she would be cared for.
When Jesus therefore had received the vinegar, he said: It is finished: and he bowed his head, and gave up the ghost.
Jesus, thank you for the cross. What I could not carry, you carried. What I could not pay, you finished. Amen.
In the end of the sabbath, as it began to dawn toward the first day of the week, came Mary Magdalene and the other Mary to see the sepulchre.
For the angel of the Lord descended from heaven, and came and rolled back the stone from the door, and sat upon it.
And the angel said unto the women: Fear not ye: for I know that ye seek Jesus, which was crucified. He is not here: for he is risen, as he said.
Mary stood weeping in the garden, until someone spoke her name. Jesus saith unto her: Mary. She turned herself, and saith unto him: Rabboni; which is to say, Master.
Risen Lord, call me by name, as you called Mary. Wherever I am weeping tonight, let me turn and find you standing there. Amen.
For forty days he showed himself alive, by many infallible proofs. Then he led them out to a mountain in Galilee.
Go ye therefore, and teach all nations. And, lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world. Amen.
And while they beheld, he was taken up; and a cloud received him out of their sight.
This same Jesus, which is taken up from you into heaven, shall so come in like manner as ye have seen him go into heaven. The story is not over.
Lord Jesus, you were born for me, you lived for me, you died for me, and you rose for me. Stay with me, as you promised, to the end. Amen.
